The FOMC’s March 20, 2019 statement delivered a dovish pause, holding the target range at 2.25–2.50% and emphasizing patience amid slower household spending/business investment and muted inflation; market-based inflation compensation remains low, and implementation (IOR at 2.40%) is consistent with the floor system.

Beige Book insights for January–February corroborate a strong labor market but softer activity: employment increased across districts with persistent worker shortages (notably in IT, manufacturing, trucking, restaurants, construction) and rising wages for both low- and high-skilled positions. At the same time, consumer spending was damped by harsh winter weather and higher credit costs; auto sales and parts of retail softened; residential real estate cooled; and manufacturing reported headwinds from weaker global demand, tariffs, and trade policy uncertainty. The government shutdown also weighed on activity. These qualitative reports align with SLOOS evidence of tighter credit standards and softer loan demand, reinforcing the FOMC’s patient stance.

Market take: duration supported by the dovish pause and muted inflation; risk assets only marginally supported given Beige Book and SLOOS headwinds in consumption, housing, and manufacturing. Adjusting for the Beige Book, the net tone moves closer to neutral than initially assumed.
